t: Within 45 days after the end of each month, the Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Homeland Security shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives a monthly budget and staffing report for that month that includes total obligations, on-board versus funded full-time equivalent staffing levels, and the number of contract employees for each office of the Department.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a mandatory, formal report is a procedural consultation requirement. But the report runs from a federal official (the DHS Chief Financial Officer) to congressional committees, and both are inside the federal government. No state, tribe, company, expert, or member of the public is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge any federal decision. The reference to contract employees is only a staffing figure to be counted, not an outside-party process.
fable.s: the Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Homeland Security shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives a monthly budget and staffing report

qwen_block.w: This section requires a federal official (the Chief Financial Officer) to submit a report to Congress (the Committees on Appropriations). According to the definition, Congress is inside the federal government, and reports to Congress are explicitly excluded from the definition of participation. There is no involvement of outside parties such as the public, states, or private entities in the decision-making process described.
qwen_block.s: the Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Homeland Security shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives a monthly budget and staffing report

opus.w: The only interaction here is a monthly budget and staffing report from a federal official to congressional committees. Both sides are inside the federal government, so nothing crosses the federal boundary. No states, experts, members of the public or other outside parties are consulted, and there is no comment period, hearing or right to sue. The required reporting looks procedural, but it is not participation.
opus.s: the Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Homeland Security shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives a monthly budget and staffing report
opus.b: The tempting reading is that a required monthly report to the Appropriations Committees is formal, procedural interaction that counts as participation. It doesn't, because Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, and the definition lists reports to Congress as a "No" trap.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the submission of a report to Congressional committees. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Therefore, this is intra-governmental reporting, not participation with outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: the Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Homeland Security shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives a monthly budget and staffing report
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the report is submitted to Congressional committees, it involves an external check or oversight, thus constituting participation. However, the definition explicitly states that "Congress, its committees and members... are all INSIDE the federal government." Therefore, reporting to Congress is intra-governmental communication, not participation with outside parties.
